jobs.label: Vétéran industriel
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE original game-ready-looking sprite study, a complete adult male cyberpunk melee fighter of the BASTION class, on genuine transparent background. This is an art-direction candidate for a 64 by 64 pixel roguelike, not a character concept illustration. Single whole figure from crown to boot soles, no captions, no grid, no props, no floor or shadow. Reference image is ONLY identity guidance: mature square-jawed brown-haired man, strong compact torso, mechanical augmentation over his anatomical right eye. Do not reuse the reference's pose, thick comic outlines, torn orange collar, pale vest, scattered buckles, or detailed fabric texture. Redesign the complete outfit coherently, including its compact default head protection, upper and lower body, sleeves, gloves and boots, all in one drawing. Facing almost front with a subtle game-like elevated view, matching classic roguelike actors rather than an isometric diamond. Sturdy broad stance, naturally bent elbows, empty hands separated from torso, feet visibly separate, no held weapon. Natural short neck seated in the shoulders. Normal compact head, no huge helmet, no exaggerated tiny head. Six to six-and-a-half heads tall, adult anatomy, no toy/chibi proportions. Full figure must read when reduced to about 58 pixels tall and 33-36 pixels wide inside a 64 pixel cell. Every large armor part has a functional, clearly shaped volume, no panel confetti, no rows of rivets, no tiny tubing. Strong upper-left light, clear but restrained material differences and large shadow shapes. Broad color areas with value contrast, no glow aura, no white sticker edge, no thick black outlines around every piece.
Art direction A: classic dark action-RPG sprite craftsmanship, carefully painted compact game sprite, weathered industrial steel rather than a superhero suit. A handsome coherent asymmetric armor design: one broad battered warm-grey steel shoulder guard on his left shoulder, a single forged dark copper breastplate with a clear beveled top edge, charcoal padded sleeves, a solid low belt, olive-grey reinforced trousers, broad steel kneecaps and heavy worn leather boots. The right upper arm is less armored to give mobility and a readable silhouette; forearm bracers are broad rather than segmented. Short fitted open-face steel brow cap and cheek guards, the face and chin remain legible. No high collar obscuring anatomy. Chest is the focal mass, head is a simple secondary highlight. Rich restrained petrol-dark shadows and desaturated warm metal highlights. Draw in economical clean painted value planes, not photo textures. Edge control should be beautiful at the tiny target size: sharp focal edges, broader quiet areas, a few deliberate chips only. It should feel like a battle-worn, believable cyberpunk brawler from a classic PC RPG, with gravity and material weight. The drawing must be conceived at native 64px, with only details that survive there.

Art direction B: crisp carefully authored pixel-art game sprite, use deliberately shaped pixel clusters and an economical cohesive palette, rendered as if a true 64 by 64 sprite has been enlarged with nearest-neighbor. No soft digital-paint blur, no tiny high-resolution outlines, no smooth illustration, no dithering noise. A strong graphic angular silhouette: an integrated flat dark navy pressure undersuit, a broad ochre-orange wedge-shaped armored chest, two squared slate-grey shoulder caps held close to the body, heavy ochre forearm guards, a narrow unadorned dark belt, solid dark trousers with one broad grey thigh protection on each leg, broad angular ochre shin guards and charcoal boots. The chest is a single broad visually calm block rather than many panels. Muscular human body under practical near-future impact armor, not a robot and not a space marine. Head wears a low-profile slate-grey close-fitting combat helmet with exposed lower face and a small blue cybernetic right eye, no huge visor. The head and torso should be part of one compact silhouette, neck barely visible. Use broad readable planes and elegant clustered highlights; roughly three tones per main material. One clear dominant orange mass and strong navy/grey counter-mass. The appeal should come from intentional shapes, confident pose and color design, not surface detailing.
